Build a stable colour palette for a sample variable

Source: R/palette_sam_pq.R
palette_sam_pq.Rd

The sample_data counterpart of palette_tax_pq(): assigns a colour to each level of a sample variable, so that a modality keeps the same colour across every figure of a document even when a subset does not contain it.

Usage

palette_sam_pq(
  physeq,
  var,
  type = "auto",
  order_by = "levels",
  nested = NULL,
  palette = "auto",
  add = c(`NA` = "grey85"),
  reorder = FALSE,
  alternate_lightness = FALSE,
  lightness_amount = 0.15,
  l_range = c(0.35, 0.82),
  on_duplicate = "parent",
  add_to_phyloseq = FALSE,
  suffix = "_color",
  force = FALSE
)

Arguments

physeq

(phyloseq, required) A phyloseq object with sample_data.

var

(character, required) A variable name from phyloseq::sample_variables().

type

(character, default "auto") "auto", "qualitative" or "sequential". See Details.

order_by

(character, default "levels") "levels" honours factor levels and falls back to alphabetical order otherwise, "frequency" sorts by decreasing number of samples, "alpha" sorts alphabetically.

nested

(character, default NULL) Name of a parent sample variable (for instance "Region" for var = "Site"). Hue then encodes the parent and lightness the level within it.

palette

(character, default "auto") "auto" picks the smallest colourblind-safe IdEst palette that fits. For type = "sequential" only the first colour is used, as the hue of the ramp; pass a single hex value to choose that hue explicitly.

add

(character, default c("NA" = "grey85")) Named reserved entries appended after the levels.

reorder

(logical, default FALSE) Reassign the colours to maximise contrast between consecutive levels. Meaningless for type = "sequential", where it is refused, and for nested.

alternate_lightness

(logical, default FALSE) Alternately lighten and darken levels. Refused for type = "sequential" and for nested.

lightness_amount

(numeric, default 0.15) Size of that alternation.

l_range

(numeric, default c(0.35, 0.82)) Lightness bounds of the sequential ramp, or of each parent's gradient when nested is supplied.

on_duplicate

(character, default "parent") See palette_tax_pq(). Only used when nested is supplied.

add_to_phyloseq

(logical, default FALSE) Write the colours into sample_data and return the phyloseq object instead of the palette.

suffix

(character, default "_color") Appended to var to build the column name.

force

(logical, default FALSE) Overwrite an existing colour column.

Value

A pq_palette (a named character vector) when add_to_phyloseq = FALSE, or the modified phyloseq object when it is TRUE.

Two kinds of variable

Sample variables split into two families that deserve different colours, and type = "auto" tells them apart:

  • qualitative (default for unordered factors and character columns): distinct hues at constant lightness, drawn from the IdEst palettes.

  • sequential (default for ordered factors and numeric columns): a single hue with increasing lightness, which reads as a gradient. Use it for sampling time, depth, pH – anything where the order carries meaning and a rainbow would destroy it.

Level order

order_by = "levels" honours the levels of a factor, so a variable declared as factor(x, levels = c("T0", "SS", "Inoc")) colours in that order rather than alphabetically. This matters most for type = "sequential", where the order is the message. Non-factor columns fall back to alphabetical order, which has the advantage of being stable when a modality disappears.

Where the palette lives

Exactly as in palette_tax_pq(): add_to_phyloseq = TRUE writes a <var><suffix> column into sample_data and returns the phyloseq object, an existing column is read back rather than recomputed, suffix lets a second palette coexist, and force overwrites.

See also

palette_tax_pq() for taxonomic ranks, show_palette_pq() to check a palette, scale_fill_sam_pq() to apply one.

Author

Adrien Taudière

Examples

# \donttest{
data(data_fungi_mini, package = "MiscMetabar")

# Qualitative: one hue per modality
palette_sam_pq(data_fungi_mini, "Height")
#> Using the colourblind-safe "Hokusai3" IdEst palette for 3 levels.
#> <pq_palette> Height: 3 levels
#>   High    #95c36e
#>   Low     #5a97c1
#>   Middle  #295384
#>   NA      grey85

# Sequential: a single hue, lightness carrying the order
palette_sam_pq(data_fungi_mini, "Time", type = "sequential")
#> <pq_palette> Time: 4 levels
#>   0   #103B6A
#>   5   #3D679A
#>   10  #6A96CC
#>   15  #9AC8FF
#>   NA  grey85
# }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Store the anchoring inside the object
ps <- palette_sam_pq(data_fungi_mini, "Height", add_to_phyloseq = TRUE)
} # }
